persona: Medical resident coordinating a small drug efficacy trial, data entered across multiple shifts from paper forms
source_style: manually transcribed from paper CRFs into Excel by different team members, then exported as CSV

columns.name: SubjectID
columns.notes: Mixed formats: S-101, S102, S-103, JD, initials; true canonical: S-101 through S-110

columns.name: Enrollment_Date
columns.notes: Three different date formats in file: YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, DD-Mon-YYYY; canonical: YYYY-MM-DD

columns.name: Baseline_Response_0-10
columns.notes: Scale 0-10; one subject has 'medium' (text); canonical is numeric

columns.name: Week2_Response
columns.notes: Numeric on same 0-10 scale; one subject has 'medium-low' (text)

columns.name: Week4_Resp_%
columns.notes: Percentage improvement 0-50%; one missing value; written as '45%', '~30%'

columns.name: Week8_Response_scale
columns.notes: Ordinal: Minimal(1)/Mild(2)/Moderate(3)/Good(4)/Marked(5); also written in parens as (1/5) etc; canonical: Minimal, Mild, Moderate, Good, Marked

columns.name: Dose_mg
columns.notes: Dose in mg; written as 100, 0.1g (=100mg), 150, 100-150 (=125 mid-point); one written as '75mg'

columns.name: Adverse_Event
columns.notes: No / Yes with description; possible values: No, Headache, Nausea, Dizziness, Rash

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: Free text; includes markers like 'DUPLICATE', 'lost to follow-up', 'Discontinued'

clean_table.reason: original clean_table was a broken Wave-1 oracle: it contained a literal '... (5 more rows)' list element and coerced values the reader will NOT (Dose_mg 0.1g->100, Week4 ~30%->30, month-name dates). See gen_h1_2.expect.json (authored from bytes) for the authoritative oracle.

intended_analysis: What is the correlation between dose and treatment response? Do adverse events predict poor response? What dose is optimal?
mess_applied: Three different date formats (YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, DD-Mon-YYYY) mixed within same column
Units inconsistently placed: '0.1g' instead of '100 mg', '75mg' attached to number
Subject IDs in different formats: S-101, S102, S-103, JD (initials), inconsistent hyphenation
Response data in three different scales: 0-10 numeric, percentage, and 5-level ordinal with codes in parens
One near-duplicate entry (S-104 appears twice with slight variation)
Missing data: Week 4 response for S-103, baseline for S-110
Free text where numeric expected: 'medium', 'medium-low' for baseline/week2 responses
Ordinal categories written inconsistently: 'Moderate (3/5)' vs 'Moderate' vs 'Mild (2/5)'
Empty notes cells vs filled cells with varying detail levels
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Treating response scales as directly comparable (0-10 vs % vs ordinal); not recognizing S-104 duplicate; parsing dose as text and missing the mg unit; treating missing baseline for S-110 as zero instead of missing.
_corrections: clean_table replaced with a superseded-by pointer (was broken).
